chunks: I said: A deceased person and a person in janabah come together in one place where there is no water except an amount sufficient for only one of them. Which of the two has more right that the water be assigned to him?
He said: “The junub performs tayammum, and the deceased is washed with water.”
From his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

“Ghusl is for janabah, the day of Jumu'ah, the day of al-Fitr, the day of al-Adha, the day of 'Arafah at the sun’s decline, for one who has washed a deceased person, when one enters into ihram, upon entering Makkah and al-Madinah, upon entering the Ka'bah, the ghusl of ziyarah, and the three nights of the month of Ramadan.”

key_terms.الزِّيَارَةِ: visitation, for which a ritual bath is mentioned here
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath performed for purification or prescribed occasions
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person who is to be ritually washed
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: to perform dry ablution in place of water-based purification
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: When water is limited between a deceased person and a junub, who should receive it, and on which occasions is ghusl performed?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings related to ghusl, tayammum, and priority in the use of limited water. It also enumerates several occasions on which ghusl is prescribed or recommended, including janabah, Jumu'ah, Eid days, 'Arafah, ihram, and ziyarah.
